chars.text: Same causes as commands.lines — the contract fields are prose-heavy by design (a falsifiable exit criterion costs a sentence, not a token), so chars grew far harder than lines. lines.text: 2026-08-12-disclosure-implement-story, the Phase 10 progressive-disclosure pilot (ADR-021, amended 2026-08-12). This is a TRANSFER, not growth: commands/implement-story.md fell 989 -> 340 lines and 52,709 -> 24,837 chars in the same change, and the eight extracted skills carry that procedure. The skills surface rises 932 -> 1814 lines (+882) while commands falls by 649 lines; the net product-line delta is +233, which is per-skill scaffolding (frontmatter + Title + Purpose + When to Use + How to Apply, ~900-1,000 bytes per file across eight files). Skills: story-context-assembly, dependency-context-loading, boundary-map-computation, change-surface-classification, drift-triage, what-was-built-authoring, project-context-snapshot, story-commit-provenance. Five sibling disclosure specs will add more; MAX_SKILLS = 12 is already exceeded at 14 and its raise belongs to 2026-08-12-governor-enforcement.

chars.text: Same cause as skills.lines. Chars relocated out of commands/implement-story.md: -27,872. Chars added to skills: +36,005 (eight files, 36,006 bytes measured by wc -c). The ~8,100-char excess over the transfer is measured per-skill scaffolding and is the pilot's headline finding for ADR-021's 2026-11-11 review trigger: extraction bought a -35.9% floor on this command and cost a +9.7% full-path ceiling, and the overhead is the whole cost. The input for the remaining five specs is fewer, larger skills. Every Compression Ledger target landed (~4,230 chars, five of six beat projection) plus ~3,974 chars of further prose compression; no rule was deleted to reduce this number. --update-baseline was deliberately NOT run: it would move every surface's floor and erase the commands justifications recorded on 2026-08-11.

2026-08-12-governor-enforcement Story 7: the identical false first-consumer sentence in adapters/cursor.md, adapters/claude-code.md and adapters/openclaw.md. All three stated that Phase 10 progressive disclosure is required_skills:'s first consumer; the phase rejected the mechanism, so the claim is permanently false in three more places than the one the ruling named. Each now records that the convention has NO consumer, why (eager pre-load moves bytes into the floor), that the phase loads skills with an inline Read at the point of need instead, and the restored 2026-11-11 review trigger with its terms. Each adapter's DESCRIPTION of the harness mechanism is accurate and is byte-unchanged — the harness genuinely does pre-load declared skills before the consumer's first phase, and that fact is what the escalation rested on. Correcting one file and leaving three would have been worse than correcting none: a reader who finds the corrected system-instructions.md and then reads an adapter gets the retired claim back, with more confidence for having seen it twice.

lines.text: a5c5a66 (install.sh/update.sh/unlink.sh runtime fan-out, PR #34, v0.28.0), 9b65a94 (scripts/eval-loop-bounds.py), and 2026-08-11-governor-instrumentation Stories 1 and 3-7 — the bound-justification reader, the emission seam, the component-contract, `## Completion`, loop-bound and required_skills: checks, and the flip-seam proof, with scripts/tests/test_eval_leanness_contract.py (81 cases) carrying most of the delta. Raised 2026-08-12: scripts/measure-invocation.py + its 20-case test suite (per-invocation load measurement, the prerequisite for progressive disclosure's success criterion, which the roadmap requires be 'measured per-invocation load, not just file size' and which nothing measured). Raised 2026-08-12: measure-invocation.py corrected to model BOTH skill load mechanisms after Phase 10 spec authoring proved required_skills: is an eager pre-load, not conditional — the old floor understated real load by 44,580 bytes across 6 commands. Raised 2026-08-12: measure-invocation.py gained placement enforcement (a hoisted inline Read is eager loading in conditional syntax and nothing else detects it) and an explicit ceiling-is-an-envelope label. Raised 2026-08-12 by 2026-08-12-governor-enforcement Story 1 (the METRIC bridge): eval.sh's check_leanness() TSV bridge printed a fixed METRIC set with no branch for contract_compliance or required_skills_declarations, so both reached the JSON and never the report a maintainer reads — grep -c over a generated report returned 0 for each. Adds guarded branches for both (plus the keys Stories 2 and 7 introduce) and scripts/tests/test_governor_enforcement.py, which extracts the shipped heredoc rather than re-typing it so a passing copy cannot hide a broken original. Raised 2026-08-12 by Story 2 (the absolute per-invocation byte cap): COMMAND_BYTE_BUDGET = 24960 with its derivation pinned at the constant, check_command_budget(), check_budget_derivation(), command_byte_sizes(), per_command_invocation() and the inline-read parser they share, plus 17 test cases. ADR-021 reason 3 asked for a ceiling alongside the ratchet, not in place of it; this is that ceiling, shipped measured and non-blocking per the 2026-08-12 (d) rescope because five commands remain over budget with no owner converting them. Raised 2026-08-12 by Story 3 (retire the check_length command limit): the 2000-line limit was 2.02x the largest command in the tree and could never bind (ADR-021 reason 1, re-measured). Replaced per ADR-021's 2026-08-12 amendment with a 400-line NON-BINDING tripwire that names COMMAND_BYTE_BUDGET as the limit that actually binds, plus three test scenarios in test_eval_length_caps.sh (401 fires as a note, 400 is legal, and the retired 2000 is asserted absent). The pointer comment is the bulk of the delta and is deliberate: a maintainer who trips a line tripwire must not be left believing lines are the budget. Raised 2026-08-12 by Story 4 (the compliance pre-check gate): ComplianceGateTests in scripts/tests/test_governor_enforcement.py — seven committed assertions against the REAL repo, one per precondition the flip depends on. 'We checked before flipping' is a hope; a committed assertion keeps guarding after the flip lands. Includes the empty-tree guard (every element of an empty list is under budget, and a vacuous green would license a flip against a tree nobody measured) and the required_skills: assertion cross-checked by a direct frontmatter grep so a parse_skill_names() change cannot make it vacuous. Raised 2026-08-12 by Story 5 (throw the severity flip): CONTRACT_CHECK_SEVERITY = "structural". The one-line diff is the smallest part — the delta is the rewritten handoff comment (the flip's date, the precondition Story 4 measured, ADR-020 'Enforcement sequencing', ADR-021 reason 2, what an un-flip would mean, and what this constant does NOT govern), five inverted seam tests, and two re-anchored string-matching tests. The two anchors are the substantive repair: both partitioned on the literal CONTRACT_CHECK_SEVERITY = "warnings", which survives the flip inside the comment's own diff preview, so each silently stopped asserting anything. Both now anchor on the assignment statement and both were proven to go red when their property is broken. Raised 2026-08-12 by Story 6 (the mutation proof): scripts/tests/test_governor_mutation.py, 12 cases. A green suite is equally consistent with a working gate and one that quietly stopped asserting anything — which is exactly what Story 5 found in two tests. Each gated property is broken on a REAL command or agent file in a scratch copy of the product surface, run through the REAL eval.sh, asserted on its exact verdict and finding text, and reverted. Includes the two mutations that test the ABSENCE of a silencing path (a planted bound justification and a planted eval-exempt: marker, neither of which reaches the byte budget) and an assertion that eval-loop-bounds.py's governor-boundary-intact scenario still PASSES rather than silently SKIPping. Raised 2026-08-12 by Story 7 (MAX_SKILLS and the mechanism record): MAX_SKILLS 12 -> 45, derived as MAX_COMMANDS + MAX_AGENTS and never from the roster, with the derivation, its date, the measured corpus, the headroom, the counterfactual and the warn-only decision recorded at the constant; and check_required_skills() extended to resolve inline `Read skills/<name>/SKILL.md` occurrences, which are the phase's actual loading mechanism and had NO resolution check at all — a mistyped one was a silent no-op that cost a capability with nothing failing anywhere. Adds the inline_skill_reads metric beside the permanently-zero required_skills_declarations, 13 test cases, and mutation I to the mutation proof. Also Story 7: two scenarios in scripts/tests/test_eval_leanness.sh were repaired for consequences of Story 5's flip and Story 2's derivation check. Scenario 4a ('a decreased surface must not warn') now counts RATCHET warnings only — every fixture root has a synthetic tiny system-instructions.md, so check_budget_derivation() correctly reports base drift there, and suppressing that check on a small base would be the wrong fix. Scenario 4e ('count ceilings stay warn-only') now builds CONTRACT-COMPLIANT extra commands: its bare `# Extra n` stubs got their structural:[] for free while the contract checks were non-blocking, so post-flip it would have asserted one thing and measured another.

2026-08-12-governor-enforcement Story 7: the `required_skills:` status paragraph. The 2026-08-03 review trigger resolved revisit-to-adopt on a justification that consisted almost entirely of a named future consumer — Phase 10 progressive disclosure — and that consumer then evaluated the mechanism and rejected it, because required_skills: is an EAGER pre-load: the harness loads every declared skill before any phase work begins, so extraction under it moves bytes into the floor and a disclosed command costs MORE per invocation than the monolith it replaced. Three claims in that paragraph were false and are corrected: Phase 10 is not the first consumer, it does not need the mechanism, and its extraction work lands ZERO declarations. The schema and the graceful-degradation rule are byte-unchanged — deprecation is ADR-scale and belongs to the review, not to the spec that discovered the problem. The delta is the measured reason with its two sources plus a restored 2026-11-11 review trigger with its terms, aligned to ADR-021's own review so one reading answers both. A resolution whose premise turned out false should not survive as a settled adoption; 2026-08-11-retire-dead-prescription exists because this repo has that failure mode.

note: Down is free. An increase to a gated surface is silent only up to a recorded ceiling: set surfaces.<name>.justifications.<lines|chars> to {"value": <measurement>, "date": "YYYY-MM-DD", "text": "<why>"}. It silences growth to that value and nothing beyond it. Rerunning --update-baseline instead moves EVERY surface's floor to its current measurement and records no reason.
